For the last seven years going into work before 5 am has been my normal. It can be hard to be awake hours before sunrise but it has always meant have more of the day left for me. My boss told me I don’t have to be at work until 545 am tomorrow. So happy for a delayed start!

After two months through the application process I finally heard back. I’m pleased to announce that I got the job! Praise be to Jesus! Thank you to everyone who kept me in your prayers. God is so good!

Tomorrow is the last of my early morning shifts, one last time walking up before 4 am and starting my shift before 5 am. It’s wild thinking that I have been doing this for nearly seven years. Can’t wait when the new normal means waking up at 6 am and starting my shift by 8 am.
Another day of work! Second day on the new job, mostly spent onboarding in the new interactive training program. It’s a lot and not that stimulating so I am grateful for my podcasts.

My new job is really challenging my identity as an introvert. I‘ve already had one meeting today and have two more on the dockets for the remainder of the day. As the week continues I have at least two meetings a day. Here’s to moving outside of my comfort zone!
I experience it on the daily and it’s been five weeks since I started my new job. I keep praying that the thoughts will disapate, it’s my hope for the both of us.

Thank you Lord for answering my prayers and to everyone who prayed for me. I can finally say that this Saturday will be my last with my old department, I can fully dedicate myself my new position after nearly four months. I have so much to look forward to. Praise be his name!

Han Solo. I have the strongest attachment to the original trilogy characters which got strengthened further with all the books I read in the EU (before it was non-cannon). I ugly cry during his death scene and time hasn’t changed that. His death crushed me more than any other.
Isn’t it amazing how quickly time goes by? Next month brings the 15 year mark for me since graduating high school, it gets a little more daunting with each five year increment. 😅

Just experienced the strangest blast from the past today - my ex texted me for my brownie recipe saying "The brownies you made still haunt my dreams". We broke up three years ago, but I'm flattered that my baking had that lasting of an impact. That's the power of a good recipe.

Decided to attend my first convention in 2019 in a city I had never been to without knowing a single person. Bought my ticket, airfare and hotel just weeks before the event. I made a wonderful friend and has an incredible experience embracing my inner nerd.

I was raised Catholic- these books were included in our Bible and regarded as Scripture. I did not take my faith seriously as a child and adolescent so I couldn’t tell you how frequently these books were mentioned in Mass. No longer Catholic so these are not a part of my Bible.

This week kicks off my full integration into the in-person rotation at my workplace. Two days a week and three days a week every other week. Reminder to self, you won’t be able to roll out of bed right before your shift on those days. Thank you Lord for seeing me through it all.

Today was one of the best Mondays I have had since my role's definition change and reincorporation into a new workgroup. The only difference over the past week was a prayer to the Lord for a shift in perspective. Thank you Lord for helping me to see beyond the negative.

I start this month of gratitude giving thanks and praise to my Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. Thank you for saving me whilst I was still a sinner, laying your life down for mine. Lord Jesus you are the Truth, the Way and the Life. You are everything to me. Praise be your name!

Today I am thankful for a job that challenges me and an incredible group of co-workers. While every day is not easy I have been pushed outside of my comfort zone and learned so much since starting this role. I look forward to each new challenge that heads my way.

Today I am thankful that I took a leap of faith and applied for my current position near this time last year. I loved my previous position and team, but it became too comfortable. We are not meant to be stagnant. Thank you Lord for shaking things up and revitalizing my work life.
